text: Nebula are vast clouds of gas and dust in space from which new stars are born. They appear as glowing regions of gas illuminated by starlight and are often referred to as the birthplaces of galaxies. A telescope is essential for astronomers to observe and study these elusive structures, revealing intricate details of the interstellar medium. Through telescopic observations, scientists can detect the electromagnetic radiation emitted by nebula, unlocking secrets about their formation, evolution, and the complex processes that drive stellar birth.
